snip.t: | Crude Birth Rate (CBR) | (Total live births ÷ Total mid-year population) × 100,000 |
snip.s: Community Health: Principles, Concepts & Diagnosis Guide — Notes

snip.t: The Crude Birth Rate (CBR) measures the number of live births in a year per 1,000 people in a population.

qs.q: When calculating demographic indicators such as the Crude Birth Rate (CBR) or Infant Mortality Rate, what standard multiplier is applied in the formulas provided?
qs.e: The formulas for demographic indicators like CBR, CDR, Under-5 Mortality Rate, MMR, and Infant Mortality Rate in the notes all multiply the calculated fraction by 100,000.
qs.s: Community Health: Principles, Concepts & Diagnosis Guide: MCQs

qs.q: What does the General Fertility Rate specifically focus on to provide a more precise measure than the Crude Birth Rate?
o: Married couples living in urban environments
Children under the age of five years
Women of reproductive age from 15 to 49 years
Total population size including infants and the elderly
qs.e: The General Fertility Rate focuses specifically on women of reproductive age, defined as 15 to 49 years old. This provides a more precise measure of fertility than the Crude Birth Rate.
